A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite substantial redesign and renaming from LSBIR to OSIRDiff. All 12 and 15 pages are readable, including trailing figures and references. Neither contains a separate appendix; supplementary materials mentioned in the text are not included.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-rescaling experiments on four datasets, component ablations, and comparisons with JPEG compression.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, component and time-step ablations, VAE comparisons, and measured inference times and parameter counts.

M1.justification: v2 replaces adapter-conditioned iterative diffusion with one-step LoRA refinement, adding a time-step prediction module and hybrid fixed/learned scheduler. Training gains a final joint fine-tuning phase and pixel, LPIPS, and DISTS losses. The stop-gradient guidance formulation and optional latent-fusion inference procedure disappear.

E1.justification: DF2K training and evaluation on DIV2K, Urban100, CLIC2020, and DIV8K are retained. v2 adds a 4× rescaling scenario to investigate the VAE bottleneck in Section 6.1. The 8× compression scenario was already present in v1, alongside 16× and 32× rescaling.

E2.justification: The six Table 1 comparators—EDSR, RCAN, ESRGAN, IRN, HCFlow, and VQIR—remain unchanged, and JPEG comparisons are retained. v2 adds direct VAE reconstruction as a comparator in Table 3 and uses an HCFlow-based pipeline in the revised pixel-space ablation.

E3.justification: The reported training procedure changes from two stages to three phases ending in joint fine-tuning. The pixel-space control changes from downsampling-based diffusion conditioning to HCFlow reconstruction followed by VAE-based enhancement. Added protocols include fixed time-step controls at 1 and 999 and runtime tests using 1024×1024 images on an RTX 3090; the six main quality metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds fixed-time-step ablations, spatial time-step/error comparisons, time-step distributions across scales, and a 4× VAE bottleneck analysis. It removes v1's convergence and intermediate-training color-shift study, stop-gradient ablation, quantitative pixel-guidance table, and fusion-weight sweep. SD-prior, domain-converter, pixel-guidance, and JPEG analyses remain, with revisions.

E5.justification: v2 Section 5.2 and Figure 18 newly report means and variances of predicted time steps across the DIV2K validation set. These describe prediction variability, rather than uncertainty across training runs. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Every Table 1 'Ours' value changes while comparator values remain identical. For DIV2K at 16×, LPIPS changes from 0.3559 to 0.3026, while MUSIQ decreases from 67.73 to 66.31. These are results for a redesigned method with changed training, not a controlled same-configuration improvement. v2 also adds VAE and runtime outcomes and revises ablation, compression, and qualitative results.

T1.justification: v2 Section 6.1 adds a finite-precision bit-count derivation yielding a latent/image storage ratio of 1/24 and a proposed rescaling boundary of sqrt(24). v1 has no corresponding argument. The explicit affine-coupling forward/inverse equations from v1 are omitted; neither version establishes a formal reconstruction-performance bound.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion shift the central contribution from two-stage, pixel-loss-free latent reconstruction to jointly trained one-step diffusion with adaptive generative strength. Latent-space rescaling and the decoupled feature-rescaling module remain central, but time-step alignment becomes a new principal contribution.

C2.justification: v2 drops v1's explanation that combining pixel and latent losses causes artifacts, and introduces explanations based on spatially varying degradation and adaptive time steps. Limitations expand to VAE reconstruction capacity and model size, supported by new comparisons. The LR-quality caveat is retained in Section 4.2.2, reframed around ringing artifacts rather than removed.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's 200K-iteration schedule, initial 2×10^-4 learning rate, 50K-step halving schedule, Adam settings, and batch size of 32, referring instead to supplementary details absent from the supplied PDF. The specific LSBIR repository address becomes an xxx/xxx placeholder. New disclosures include tiled inference and the hardware and image resolution used for timing.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 substantially expands positioning around diffusion acceleration and distillation, discussing progressive distillation, InstaFlow, Diffusion2GAN, and LoRA. Additional restoration work supports the new limitations discussion, while the T2I-Adapter citation disappears. The earlier image-rescaling literature is largely retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution narrative, perceptual-enhancement methodology, and analysis sections undergo substantial rewriting. Discussions become a standalone section, fusion discussion is replaced by time-step analysis, and Limitations gains two subsections. The title, method acronym, and author list also change.

P2.justification: The framework diagram is extensively redrawn, the pixel/latent comparison is reworked and moved into the ablations, and qualitative grids are replaced or expanded. Convergence and fusion displays disappear, while refiner, time-step, VAE-comparison, and runtime displays are added. Table 1 largely retains its original structure.

improvement.justification: v2 provides better evidence about the redesigned method's behavior and practical costs through fixed-time-step controls, spatial analyses, and runtime/model-size comparisons. These improve assessability beyond the changed benchmark scores. The net gain is limited by loss of explicit training settings and a specific repository address, while the new VAE 'upper bound' remains an argument rather than an established performance bound.
